_meta.indication: EGRIFTA is a growth hormone releasing factor (GRF) analog indicated for the reduction of excess abdominal fat in HIV-infected patients with lipodystrophy.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled 26-week Main Phase (2:1 randomization) followed by a randomized withdrawal Extension Phase.
pivotal_trials.population: HIV-infected patients with lipodystrophy and excess abdominal fat accumulation.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Percent change from Baseline to Week 26 in visceral adipose tissue (VAT) measured by CT.
pivotal_trials.result: VAT % change -17.8% tesamorelin vs +2.2% placebo; treatment difference -19.6% (95% CI -23.7, -15.3), p<0.001.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled 26-week Main Phase (2:1 randomization) followed by a randomized withdrawal Extension Phase.
pivotal_trials.population: HIV-infected patients with lipodystrophy and excess abdominal fat accumulation.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Percent change from Baseline to Week 26 in visceral adipose tissue (VAT) measured by CT.
pivotal_trials.result: VAT % change -13.8% tesamorelin vs -2.4% placebo; treatment difference -11.7% (95% CI -16.2, -7.1), p<0.001.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>5% and more frequent than placebo): arthralgia, injection site erythema, injection site pruritis, pain in extremity, peripheral edema, and myalgia. Key warnings include elevated IGF-I (47.4% with IGF-I SDS >2 at 26 weeks), glucose intolerance/diabetes, fluid retention, and injection site reactions (24.5% vs 14.4% placebo).
target_moa: Tesamorelin is a synthetic analog of human growth hormone releasing factor (GRF/GHRF) that stimulates the release of pituitary growth hormone.

rems.type: DRISK concluded that a REMS is not warranted as the review of available safety information for Egrifta did not identify safety concerns not already known with growth hormone products, none of which has a REMS.

advisory_committee.vote: At the May 27, 2010 EMDAC meeting, all 16 voting members voted 'yes' that the overall risk-benefit assessment supports approval; there were no abstentions.

basis.text: Application was a Standard review, not Priority.

summary.text: Egrifta was approved under a standard NDA review (submitted May 29, 2009) following a unanimous (16-0) favorable EMDAC advisory committee vote on May 27, 2010; approval was supported by two Phase 3 trials meeting the primary VAT reduction endpoint, with three postmarketing required studies and no REMS.

citations.quote: All 16 voting members voted 'yes' to this question. There were no abstentions.
Egrifta clearly met its primary efficacy endpoint in two pivotal studies.

DRISK has concluded that a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) is not warranted as their review of available safety information for Egrifta did not identify safety concerns not already known with growth hormone products, none of which has a REMS.

requirement.text: 1708-1: Manufacturing studies to determine a process for providing a daily dose (2 mg) of lyophilized product in a single vial to replace the two-vial container-closure system.

citations.quote: 1708-1 Manufacturing studies to determine a process for providing a daily dose (2 mg) of lyophilized product in a single vial. This single vial would replace the container-closure system described in the original application in which the daily dose is provided in two separate vials each containing 1.1 mg of lyophilized powder.

requirement.text: 1708-2: A long-term observational safety study of at least 10 years duration comparing Egrifta-treated vs untreated HIV-associated lipodystrophy patients to assess long-term safety concerns (glucose intolerance/diabetes, hypersensitivity, malignancies, liver/kidney abnormalities, diabetic retinopathy, and MACE).

citations.quote: 1708-2 A long-term observational safety study of at least 10 years duration comparing patients with HIV-associated lipodystrophy and excess abdominal fat treated with Egrifta compared to a similar group of patients not treated with Egrifta to assess potential safety concerns associated with long-term administration of Egrifta, including but not limited to the occurrence of glucose intolerance/diabetes mellitus, hypersensitivity reactions, malignancies, liver abnormalities, kidney abnormalities, diabetic retinopathy, and major adverse cardiovascular events.

requirement.text: 1708-3: A prospective, randomized, placebo-controlled clinical trial to evaluate whether Egrifta increases the risk of development or progression of diabetic retinopathy in HIV-infected patients with lipodystrophy and concomitant diabetes, also evaluating long-term glucose metabolism and MACE.
